name: The Hundred
description: Supine breathing and abdominal endurance exercise with the trunk curled, legs held in a controlled position, and the arms pumping rhythmically.
teaching_cues: Draw the abdominals inward and keep the pelvis stable.
Reach the legs away only as low as trunk control allows.
Pump the arms from the shoulders while keeping the neck long.
Coordinate five arm pumps with the inhale and five with the exhale.
common_mistakes: Losing abdominal support and arching the lower back.
Tensing the shoulders or pulling the chin into the chest.
Lowering the legs beyond the point of control.

restrictions.modification: Keep the head supported or lower it to the mat and reduce cervical flexion.
Keep the legs higher or bent in tabletop to reduce the lever.
Later-pregnancy supine work may need an alternative position and instructor-specific modification.

progressions: Lower the straight legs while maintaining trunk and pelvic control.
Add a light prop such as a magic circle or small ball without changing alignment.
regressions: Use tabletop legs or feet supported.

name: Roll Up
description: Controlled spinal articulation from supine to seated and back, using the abdominals to sequence the spine rather than momentum.
teaching_cues: Initiate from the abdominals and articulate one spinal segment at a time.
Keep the legs long and grounded without gripping.
Reach forward through the crown of the head at the top.
Control the return instead of dropping to the mat.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to sit up.
Feet lifting from the mat.
Collapsing the shoulders or yanking the arms forward.

restrictions.modification: Use an approved neutral-spine alternative instead of loaded spinal flexion.
Use a smaller range or assistance such as a strap and avoid forcing the roll.
Slightly bend the knees or elevate the hips if needed.

progressions: Slow the articulation and reduce arm momentum.
Perform with arms overhead through more of the range.
regressions: Use a resistance band around the feet for assistance.

name: Roll Over
description: Advanced supine inversion that rolls the pelvis and spine overhead while maintaining abdominal control and length through the legs.
teaching_cues: Lift from the abdominals rather than kicking the legs overhead.
Keep weight on the shoulder girdle, not the neck.
Lengthen the legs away as the spine articulates back to the mat.
Move with control through the entire rollover.
common_mistakes: Rolling onto the neck.
Using momentum or throwing the legs.
Collapsing the chest or losing abdominal support.

restrictions.modification: Choose a non-inverted abdominal exercise unless specifically cleared and supervised.
Use a non-inverted alternative if the shoulder girdle cannot support the position.
Use an approved neutral-spine alternative.

progressions: Increase precision of the leg opening/closing pattern while maintaining the shoulder-supported position.
regressions: Hip lift without taking the legs fully overhead.

name: Single Leg Circles
description: Supine hip-mobility exercise in which one leg circles from the hip while the pelvis and trunk remain stable.
teaching_cues: Keep both sides of the pelvis heavy and level.
Move the leg from the hip socket rather than the knee.
Make the circle only as large as pelvic stability allows.
Keep the supporting leg active and long.
common_mistakes: Rocking the pelvis side to side.
Making the circle too large.
Tensing the shoulders or bending the moving knee unintentionally.

restrictions.modification: Reduce the circle size and keep the motion comfortable.
Slightly bend the moving knee or use a strap.
Keep the non-working leg bent with the foot on the mat if needed.

progressions: Keep the non-working leg fully extended and increase the circle only without pelvic movement.
regressions: Use a strap for hamstring support.

name: Rolling Like a Ball
description: Balanced seated rolling exercise that maintains a compact C-curve while rolling to the shoulder blades and returning without using the feet.
teaching_cues: Maintain the same rounded shape throughout the roll.
Initiate the return from the abdominals rather than kicking the legs.
Roll to the shoulder blades, not onto the neck.
Balance behind the sit bones without letting the feet touch down.
common_mistakes: Throwing the head or legs to create momentum.
Flattening the spine during the roll.
Rolling onto the neck.

restrictions.modification: Keep the roll small and avoid rolling onto the cervical spine.
Choose a neutral-spine balance exercise instead.
Practice the start-position balance or a small rocking range.

progressions: Reduce the hand support while preserving the compact shape.
Transition directly into the abdominal series.
regressions: Hold behind the thighs instead of the shins.

name: Single Leg Stretch
description: Supine abdominal-series exercise alternating one knee toward the chest while the opposite leg reaches away and the trunk remains curled.
teaching_cues: Keep the pelvis stable while the legs alternate.
Reach the extending leg long rather than simply lowering it.
Keep the shoulders lifted without shortening the neck.
Switch the legs smoothly with the breath.
common_mistakes: Rocking the pelvis.
Pulling on the knee aggressively.
Letting the lower back arch as the leg reaches away.

restrictions.modification: Support or lower the head.
Keep the extending leg higher or shorten the lever.
Reduce leg reach and focus on abdominal control.

progressions: Lower the reaching leg while maintaining pelvic control.
Increase flow without losing precision.
regressions: Keep the reaching leg bent or higher.

name: Double Leg Stretch
description: Supine abdominal-series exercise extending both arms and legs away from center and circling back while the trunk remains controlled.
teaching_cues: Keep the trunk position unchanged as the limbs reach away.
Reach long through the arms and legs before circling back.
Only lower the legs as far as the abdominals can control.
Keep the shoulders broad and the neck long.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back during the reach.
Dropping the head and shoulders.
Moving too quickly to hide loss of control.

restrictions.modification: Keep the head supported or down.
Reach the legs higher or keep the knees bent.
Limit the overhead arm range.

progressions: Longer arm and leg lever with a lower leg angle while maintaining trunk control.

name: Single Straight Leg Stretch
description: Supine abdominal-series exercise alternating straight legs in a scissoring pattern while maintaining trunk flexion and pelvic control.
teaching_cues: Keep both legs long and switch from the hips.
Maintain an anchored pelvis and steady trunk curl.
Use a gentle double pulse without pulling the leg aggressively.
Keep the lower leg only as low as control allows.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees unintentionally.
Pulling the top leg with the arms.
Arching the lower back as the lower leg descends.

restrictions.modification: Bend the knees slightly or reduce the range.
Support or lower the head.
Keep the lower leg higher.

progressions: Increase the split while keeping the pelvis still.
Reduce hand assistance.

name: Double Straight Leg Stretch
description: Supine abdominal exercise lowering and lifting both straight legs together while maintaining trunk and pelvic stability.
teaching_cues: Keep the pelvis and rib cage steady as the legs lower.
Lower only to the point before the back begins to arch.
Reach the legs long away from the hips.
Use the exhale to support the return.
common_mistakes: Lowering the legs too far.
Flaring the ribs or arching the back.
Using momentum on the lift.

restrictions.modification: Reduce the lowering range or bend the knees.
Keep the head down or supported.
Shorten the lever or use bent knees.

progressions: Lower the legs farther while maintaining neutral control.
Add a light magic circle between the ankles.

name: Criss Cross
description: Rotational abdominal-series exercise alternating thoracic rotation toward the bent knee while the opposite leg reaches long.
teaching_cues: Rotate from the rib cage rather than pulling the elbow across.
Keep the pelvis stable as the legs switch.
Reach the opposite leg long.
Keep the elbows wide and the neck supported by the trunk.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the neck.
Moving only the elbows instead of rotating the torso.
Rocking the pelvis or rushing the switches.

restrictions.modification: Keep the head supported or reduce the trunk lift.
Keep the reaching leg higher and reduce range.
Use a non-rotational abdominal alternative.

progressions: Slower rotation with a longer leg reach.
Pause briefly in each rotated position.
regressions: Feet remain in tabletop with smaller leg reach.

name: Spine Stretch Forward
description: Seated spinal-flexion and axial-length exercise reaching forward over long legs while maintaining grounded sit bones.
teaching_cues: Grow tall before initiating the forward articulation.
Keep the sit bones grounded as the spine rounds.
Reach forward through the crown of the head rather than collapsing.
Stack the spine with control to return.
common_mistakes: Hinging from the hips instead of articulating the spine.
Shrugging the shoulders.
Allowing the knees to bend excessively from tension.

restrictions.modification: Use an approved neutral-spine seated hinge or axial-length exercise.
Bend the knees slightly or sit on a small elevation.
Use a smaller range and focus on axial length.

progressions: Increase articulation and reach while keeping the pelvis grounded.
regressions: Sit on a cushion or block.

name: Open Leg Rocker
description: Balanced rolling exercise with both legs extended in a V, maintaining trunk control and returning to the same balanced position.
teaching_cues: Maintain the relationship between trunk and legs as you roll.
Roll to the shoulder blades, not the neck.
Use the abdominals to stop and balance at the top.
Keep the legs active and evenly spaced.
common_mistakes: Throwing the legs to create momentum.
Collapsing the chest at the top.
Rolling onto the neck.

restrictions.modification: Reduce the roll range and avoid cervical loading.
Use a seated balance alternative.
Keep the knees slightly bent.

progressions: Straighten the knees fully and reduce reliance on the hands.

name: Corkscrew w/Hips over
description: Advanced supine/inverted leg-circle exercise combining abdominal control, spinal articulation, and a controlled hip lift.
teaching_cues: Keep the shoulders grounded and the neck free of pressure.
Circle the legs from a stable trunk and lift the hips from the abdominals.
Make both sides of the circle even.

Using momentum to lift the hips.

Use a neutral-spine alternative.
Use low corkscrew without lifting the hips.

name: Saw
description: Seated rotation and forward reach combining thoracic rotation with spinal flexion over an extended leg position.
teaching_cues: Grow tall before rotating.
Keep both sit bones grounded as you reach forward.
Rotate from the rib cage rather than shifting the pelvis.
Reach opposite hand toward the outside of the foot without collapsing.

Rounding the shoulders instead of articulating the spine.
Forcing the reach with the arms.

restrictions.modification: Use a non-rotational seated mobility exercise.
Bend the knees slightly or sit on a small elevation.
Reduce rotation and forward range.

progressions: Increase the rotation and reach while keeping the pelvis anchored.

name: Neck Roll/Swan
description: Prone spinal-extension sequence that lifts the chest through back-extensor control and may add gentle cervical rotation/neck roll at the top.
teaching_cues: Lengthen the spine before lifting into extension.
Keep the abdominals supportive and the pelvis organized.
Distribute extension through the thoracic spine rather than hinging only in the low back.

Shrugging the shoulders.
Throwing the head back or forcing neck rotation.

Omit the neck roll and keep the cervical spine long.
Use forearm support or reduce arm loading.

name: Single Leg Kicks
description: Prone forearm-supported exercise alternating knee flexion while the trunk remains lifted and stable.

Keep the pelvis stable as the heel kicks toward the seat.

name: Double Leg Kicks
description: Prone exercise combining three heel kicks toward the seat with a chest-opening extension and arm reach behind the body.

name: Neck Pull
description: Advanced roll-up variation performed with hands behind the head, requiring strong abdominal control, spinal articulation, and a controlled hip hinge.
teaching_cues: Keep the hands light and avoid pulling the head forward.

Sit tall before hinging back as one long line.
Control the descent through the spine.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the neck.
Using momentum to roll up.

Slightly bend the knees or reduce forward range.

name: High Scissors
description: Shoulder-supported inverted exercise alternately reaching one straight leg toward the mat and the other toward the body while the pelvis stays lifted.
teaching_cues: Support the pelvis with the hands while keeping weight off the neck.
Keep the pelvis high and steady as the legs switch.
Reach both legs long in opposite directions.

Reduce the leg split.

name: High Bicycle
description: Shoulder-supported inverted cycling pattern that alternates hip and knee motion while the pelvis remains elevated and stable.
teaching_cues: Keep the pelvis supported and lifted throughout the cycling action.
Reach each leg long through the bottom of the cycle.

restrictions.modification: Use a low bicycle variation or non-inverted leg exercise.

Reduce the cycling range.

name: Shoulder Bridge
description: Supine bridge held through the posterior chain while one leg extends and performs controlled kicks without dropping or rotating the pelvis.

name: High Bridge
description: Advanced high bridge variation with a larger hip and spinal extension demand, often performed with strong posterior-chain and shoulder support.
teaching_cues: Lift through the hips while keeping the chest open and the neck unloaded.
Maintain even weight through both feet and shoulders.
Lengthen the knees away from the shoulders.

restrictions.modification: Use a lower bridge variation.

name: Spine Twist
description: Seated axial-rotation exercise with the legs extended and pelvis grounded while the torso rotates around a tall vertical axis.

Keep both sit bones anchored and the legs still.
Rotate through the rib cage rather than swinging the arms.

name: Jackknife
description: Advanced inversion that rolls the legs overhead and then lifts them vertically before articulating the spine back to the mat.
teaching_cues: Roll overhead with abdominal control before lifting the legs upward.

name: Side Kicks - Front/Back
description: Side-lying hip exercise swinging the top leg forward and back while the trunk and pelvis remain stable.

name: Side Kicks - Up/Down

Keep the pelvis quiet and stacked.
Maintain length through the working leg.

Moving the pelvis with the leg.

name: Side Kicks - Bicycle

name: Side Kicks - Big Scissors
description: Advanced side-lying scissor action with both legs moving in opposition, demanding strong lateral trunk control and hip mobility.

name: Teaser 1

Teaser 3
